subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what trigger plus local editor/temp-file safety contract should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but executing `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR` and persisting prompt drafts crosses a local process and sensitive-data boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve guarded core flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, safe editor invocation, restrictive temp-file handling, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold for UX choice
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers settle the shortcut or slash-command model and reconcile the inactive external-editor keybinding entry.

options.title: Decline external handoff
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers prefer inline multiline editing, composer expansion, or another editing surface instead of launching local editors from the TUI.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded core flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, safe editor invocation, restrictive temp-file handling, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has already reviewed this exact issue and has relevant recent TUI history for the UX and safety decision.
